title: The Unity of Divine Power and the Distinction of Mercy and Judgment
english: …words, he says: “I have become like those who have been slain and lie in a tomb” (Psalm 87:6 (88:5)), who suffer this because they were separated from your life-giving power. For it is clear that this was not true of him: the body of Christ was full of the power of God even after death. That is why blood and water poured from him, though nothing of the kind comes from dead bodies.

(Psalm 87:9-10) [Another interpreter, explaining “You have made me an abomination to them,” says:] Just as the disciples were ashamed at his sufferings, no longer hoping for a Savior or redeemer—they even said, “The rulers handed him over to a sentence of death, but we had hoped that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel” (Luke 24:20-21). It is clear that he was also held fast in the hands of his enemies, handed over willingly, yet held all the same. There he came into affliction for our sake, for he bore everything that is heavy and afflicting to a body. For instead of “My eyes have grown weak from poverty” (Psalm 87:10 (88:9)), Symmachus rendered, “My eye has poured out from affliction.”

(Psalm 87:13) Save, then, the race you have made, by your own knowledge, and lead back to life the human beings who have fallen into death in either way. They must be spectators of your wonders and interpreters of your power; let them not remain overlooked in forgetfulness, but, remembered again by you, let them be led back to life. This is what the champion of human beings says, interceding for the common race of all and working out the life of the world by the will of the Father.

(Psalm 87:14) The ambassador and priest presents himself on our behalf in an unceasing presentation, from dawn and through the night, and he appeases the wrath of God against us, which he himself took upon himself in his sufferings.

(Psalm 87:16) He calls “exaltation” the exaltation in wonders and signs, about which the Father says to him, “I have glorified it” (John 12:28), when the Son says, “Glorify your Son” (John 17:1). He says this was changed into humiliation when he came to suffer, suffering for human beings and abandoned by those for whom he suffered.

(Psalm 88:13) Mount Tabor lies in the region of the Galileans, and Hermon in the desert toward Sinai. God must be hymned, he says, not only for his works around Tabor but also for the manifestation that took place around Hermon.

(Psalm 88:14-15) “Your power,” he says, “prevails. Let your strength appear; let it become manifest and glorious among human beings.” All these things he has included as spoken to one God. We know his power as one and only, an arm and a hand that is perfect. Through it all things have come into being and are coming into being, so that it, being perfect in itself, is numbered with God according to the one number of the Godhead and in no way falls under what is said about the many sons, none of whom, the word has said beforehand, is like the One who truly is. For the one true power is not like them; it is the true image and the mark of God alone, God accomplishing all things through it. Therefore the divine things were fitted to its sojourn among human beings, and the judgment of God is exercised by Christ: judgment belongs to him as the power of God but is given to him as a human being, as he himself has said. And he divided mercy and judgment by the times. Judgment he foretold from then on, for when the King comes and sits on the throne of his glory. For that throne has righteousness, as it were, for its base, as in the ninth psalm Aquila said beforehand, “He set his throne firmly in judgment” (Psalm 9:8 (9:7)). Before that manifestation there is abundant mercy on the earth, a forerunner, as it were, of his coming as judge, the fearful judge who is to appear preparing human beings beforehand for salvation by mercy. And with mercy comes truth, because nothing untrue or not upright can happen in God’s kind long-suffering, even if to those who do not know the future it seems that the wicked are wrongly allowed to prosper and that the good are unjustly overlooked when they suffer loss.

(Psalm 88:20-25) He now explicitly recounts the promise made through Nathan the prophet, indicating prophets in the plural from one, whom he also calls “sons of God,” or, as the other interpreters render it, “holy ones of God.” He says that God declared that he gave David a share of power and brought him forward to glory, having chosen him, as in the words, “I took you from the sheepfold, from following the flocks, to be ruler over my people Israel” (2 Samuel 7:8); and that, finding him pleasing, he anointed him with the holy oil for the kingship, and was present with him, working all things together with him, making the uprisings of his enemies void, cutting down their armies and putting them to flight, as in the words, “I was with you in…” (2 Samuel 7:9).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

Re-review 2026-10-09 (Densify): retranslated from the locked Greek after a clause-aligned two-family check (Workers AI kimi-k2.6 + glm-5.2) found major meaning errors in the earlier English; see reviews/fix-notes-2026-10-09-rereview.md.

title: The Seasons of Refreshment
english: To all those to whom you have gone and to whom I have destroyed all your enemies from before your face, as it is written through the prophet Nathan (Ps 88:36). And he says that he exalts him by his own mercy and with the diligence pertaining to the righteous. Just as he also unexpectedly obtained victories in wars and was invincible.

God swears by himself, because he has nothing greater by which to swear, just as Paul says. For he says, 'I have sworn by my holy [one],' or as the E edition says, 'According to my sanctification' instead of 'According to my holiness' (Ps 88:39). [These things were likewise set forth by Theodore similar to Apollinaris.]

It seems to seek something greater and beyond man (Ps 88:49), despising the life we live as being nothing, claiming that men move into something futile, not indeed into vanity, but as he deems worthy of not adding corruption, since it is clearly stated that the kingdom will be restored when even corruption is loosed and the living unto the ages is given. For where would escape from death come to us? And where, if not from you? For this would not exist for a man from himself; there is no one who will live and will not die, nor will he be able to save himself from death. But these things seek in opposition to the heavenly king, the redeemer of futility, the same who is stronger than death and a savior of men from death, transforming the futility of the present life into truth and constructing the eternal kingdom upon eternal life.

He did not reject the mercy, but seeks the promise and invokes the justice of God against the impious nations who revile the righteous, having done evil against his own race and having fallen (Ps 88:51); whom he says are enemies of God, yet revile the trace of the righteous king as if it were erased. Having urged these things, he blesses. And the blessing is of one hoping. And of one hoping, he seems to mean the prayers will reach the promise and will not fall away, just as Paul says, 'Is it possible that the word of God has fallen away?' (Rom 3:3).

If he has spoken thus concerning a thousand years (Ps 89:10), it is evident that the span of human life will be the most minute and as if indivisible. The whole, he says, human life is described in a seventy-year period.

Regarding the greater part, he says this: not even this is given in ease, but almost entirely in hardship; for either we are being instructed as infants, or we are laboring as youths, or we are being afflicted as old men. Therefore, he rightly said, 'And the greater part of them is labor and toil' (Ps 89:17). For thus, because the order according to age exists, a little time is stolen away toward joy.

Night, it is fitting, he called the whole time in which a dying man sleeps, but the first is the dawn in which we shall live, when the Lord has appeared and mercy has descended from heaven. It is worthy that the sun and day should shine forth and be given continuously to the righteous as joy instead of the days in which we were harmed, falling into countless evils. These are the Seasons of Refreshment which Peter foretells, to whom he says that our pre-appointed Jesus the Lord will be sent.

Furthermore, he says a thousand shall fall from the auspicious sides, and ten thousand from the right (Ps 90:8), before even approaching and turning away some evil, so that they fall seeing helplessly, and to the perishing he will repay from God, just as it happened to Jehoshaphat according to the promise, so that not having fought, but singing and praising God among one another, he saw the enemies being destroyed. For he says, 'They came upon the lookout of the wilderness and looked and saw the multitude, and behold, all dead having fallen upon the earth, and there was no one being saved.' Near to this also happened to other kings hoping in God, the promise of God being made true, which says, 'I will hate your enemies and I will oppose those who oppose you.' Yet it is not necessary always to think that victories are effortless for the righteous. Since even coming through battle, many times they have conquered, but regarding the most manifest in these things, he says, 'help,' in which most especially God the helper appears to be.

He brought the face of the one hoping near, saying to himself toward God that he placed his hope in him (Ps 90:9). And again he exclaims to such a one, 'Because you have chosen the Most High as a house of safety, no evil shall hold you, nor shall your house be filled with divine plagues' (Ps 90:10). For it is evident that if a righteous man suffers, and the house of a righteous man, [it is] a struggle.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Reigns and the Judgment of the Nations
english: This is not a punishment from God against those standing in injustice. It is clear that evils will not prevail against the one undergoing training, but he will rise up as if from sleep, just as it was said in the third Psalm: even if he falls seven times according to the proverb, he will rise (Ps 92:1b; Prov 24:16).

It is possible, therefore, and how much more appropriate to speak of the clothing of glory and the girding of power in relation to the knowledge concerning men, rather than regarding the dishonor of Christ's former presence and human weakness. He himself also brings forward in it the sustaining of the inhabited world for good, which can no longer be moved in any way.

He says that the unjust cannot partake of your kingdom, those who bring toil upon those guarding the laws, by whom the righteous is hunted for capture and he who does no injustice is murdered (Ps 93:20). In these things, the destruction of injustice is shown generally, being established by the justice of God. You said, 'You will not give dominion to the evil, but you will set safety for the righteous, establishing it as a refuge for him and the hopes that hold fast to you'; and what the wicked thought would proceed against the righteous, these things will turn back and upon them themselves; and just as they worked to make the righteous vanish, so they will go into vanishing. This is the end of the vengeance from you.

Let God be known, whom we revere, he who has the heaven and the glory supra-heavenly, to whom beauty is present, to whom power and majesty are in the unutterable (Ps 95:6); that is, according to the incorporeal and divine excellence, since the physical magnitudes of the temples have been granted to the bodily, and beauty to technical precision, and wealth to luxury, and to the nations concerning demons. In Israel, indeed, even if these things were present, they occurred according to a type of the invisible things from the beginning, and it is said through Moses, and it yields to the invisible; especially now during the present Gospel, when spiritual [excellence] is sought and perceived, but also the old [way] is [present] for the wise, just as with Solomon, the greatest and most luxurious, since he was the greatest, having built a temple for the God who spoke, saying that even the heaven cannot contain the glory of God. The Lord has reigned differently then and differently now, hearing (Ps 96:1)...

For indeed, from the former presence he reigned as one decisively condemning sin in the holy flesh and having abolished death. And in the second reign, through each of his partakers, having overcome evil and corruption, so that men shall finally arrive to behold the treasury of eternal life being filled with the life from him, already being able and seeing the glory of his kingdom appearing in them as in a royal house, while making the adversaries invisible as fire melts wax.

Therefore, the earth rejoices again, as it says, and the many islands, that is, the nations, are glad (Ps 96:7-8); then after that, the earth shall labor and the mountains shall melt. How does he speak of the saints, and how does he speak of the adversaries, of whom he also depicts the highness through pride as mountains, and makes the destruction of their pride like the melting of mountains? And to the strangers, he shows fear and constriction by meeting them with clouds and darkness before the sight of the Lord; but to those receptive of light, he says his lightning flashes and glory is being seen, and furthermore, the judicial fire shall consume the ungodly, the righteousness of the Lord being revealed from heaven, as the apostle says. But the psalmist says the being revealed from heaven is announced by naming the appearance of the heavens as an angel, and that he establishes the heaven by righteousness and judgment, as if speaking upon some foundation. He makes it clear that the throne is not a physical thing, but that the kingdom is called a throne.

Those who worship idols through much insensitivity and foolishness, which they themselves carved, he prays will be ashamed, having received sense. For this will turn out for good. For they will turn away, having been ashamed of this foolish notion, which they held as if they were gods.

An enemy and an adversary to God, the evil one, will not oppose a thing that is of nature (Ps 96:10). For that which is contrary to nature is not divided from the good nature, nor is it possible to find any nature which is called evil; for we do not have such a thing in our knowledge, so that knowing it we might hate it, but we recognize all evil as a work according to wickedness, and the hatred of this, if we think well, we are prepared to treat equally.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
